{{Short description|Russian physicist}}
'''Igor Viktorovich Tyutin''' ({{langx|ru|И́горь Ви́кторович Тю́тин}}, [[transliteration]]: ''{{lang|ru-Latn|Igor' Viktorovič Tyutin}}''; 24 August 1940 – 23 January 2026) was a Russian theoretical physicist, who worked on [[quantum field theory]].<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://td.lpi.ru/index_m.html
 |title=Announcement of the death of I. V. Tyutin
 |publisher=I. E. Tamm Theory Department, Lebedev Physical Institute
 |date=2026-01-23
 |language=ru
}}</ref>

Tyutin was a professor at the [[Lebedev Institute]] in [[Moscow]]. In an unpublished Lebedev Institute report, he developed the [[BRST formalism]] around 1975 in Russia in parallel to and independently of the work of  [[Carlo Becchi]],  [[:de:Alain Rouet|Alain Rouet]], and  [[Raymond Stora]] in France. The BRST formalism is a method for quantization of fields with constraints such as gauge invariance. In quantum field theory, the procedure is of fundamental importance for attempts at constructing string field theories.<ref>{{cite book|author1=Gitman, D.M.|author2=Tyutin, I.V.|title=Quantization of fields with constraints|year=1990|publisher=Springer, Berlin|isbn=3-540-51679-4}}</ref> In 2009 Tyutin received the [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]] with [[Carlo Becchi]], Alain Rouet, and [[Raymond Stora]].
